description: ADR-005 seed query set — graded relevance (0 = not relevant .. 3 = highly relevant) against contracts/fixtures/eval/corpus.json. q6 is the temporal as_of case exercising bitemporal time-travel: at as_of, atom-002 (the supersession) does not exist yet, so only atom-001 (still valid at that instant) is relevant. q9-q11 (FEAT-402 slice 2 AC-8) exercise the entity `filters.entity` pre-fusion intersection: q9/q10 use entities shared by exactly two corpus atoms so recall/NDCG floors hold trivially; q11 exercises the AC-4 exact-then-LIKE resolution ('postgres' substring-matches the 'postgresql' entity) plus the current-snapshot validity filter (atom-001 is invalidated/superseded, so only atom-002 survives).

queries.notes: Temporal case: as_of predates atom-002's valid_from (2026-06-15), so atom-001 (valid 2026-06-01..2026-06-15) is the only correct hit at this instant, not its successor.
FEAT-402 AC-4: entity=sqlite-vec pre-fusion-intersects the candidate set down to exactly the two atoms linked to the sqlite-vec entity (atom-003, atom-009) — 'all-and-only entity-linked members'.

FEAT-402 AC-4: entity=bun matches atom-004 and atom-009 (both entity-linked to 'Bun'); atom-005 ('bun run test command') is lexically related but carries no entities and MUST be excluded — proves the filter is a real intersection, not a lexical boost.

FEAT-402 AC-4/AC-9: 'postgres' has no exact entities.name match (the stored, normalized name is 'postgresql') so resolveIds falls back to a LIKE substring match. Both atom-001 and atom-002 are entity-linked, but atom-001 is invalidated (superseded) so the current-snapshot validity filter leaves only atom-002.
